## 1. The factor model

The goal is to forecast **stock-specific alpha**, isolate unwanted common bets, and control portfolio risk:

$$
R_{t,t+H}=B_t f_{t,t+H}+\epsilon_{t,t+H},\qquad
\Sigma_{t,H}=B_t\Omega_{t,H}B_t^\top+D_{t,H}.
$$

- **$B_t$:** PIT exposures to market, industries, and style factors; **$f$:** realized factor returns; **$\epsilon$:** residual returns.
- **Alpha:** predict $\widehat E_t[\epsilon_{t,t+H}]$, not an automatically profitable signal.
- **Neutrality:** $B_t^\top P_t=0$ implies $P_t^\top R=P_t^\top\epsilon$ for fixed holdings and the *same* factor decomposition. In practice, neutralize the most important factors and bound others; neutralizing everything may eliminate useful positions.
- **Risk:** use $P_t^\top\widehat\Sigma_{t,H}P_t$ in the optimizer; residual positions still have risk.

**Residual construction:** Freeze $B_t$ at the decision time; *after* each 30-minute interval, estimate matching factor returns via cross-sectional WLS and set $\widehat\epsilon=R-B_t\widehat f$. Only completed labels enter training. Daily factor returns cannot directly residualize 30-minute returns.

## 2. Why a comprehensive model rather than a naive one?

**Simple models are useful benchmarks, but too incomplete for the primary residual-definition and risk-control system.** The key concern is **omitted common risk being misclassified as alpha**.

| Failure in a simple model | Concrete consequence for SAF | Needed capability |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Market beta only; no industry factors** | Long semiconductor / short utilities can be market-neutral yet lose sharply in a sector rotation. Sector returns enter the *supposedly stock-specific* residual labels. | Market **+ industry** exposures. |
| **No style factors** | A hidden Momentum, Size, Value, or Volatility bet can masquerade as persistent alpha; optimizer concentrates that exposure. | Selected **style factors**, tested for incremental relevance. |
| **Independent residuals by assumption** | With 20 equal-weight stocks, residual correlation $\rho=0.4$ makes portfolio variance **8.6×** the diagonal-only prediction ($1+(20-1)\rho$), under equal volatilities. | **Specific risk** plus possible residual correlations / shrinkage. |
| **Static or backfilled exposures** | Today's loadings applied in 2015 create look-ahead bias; stale beta misses changes in business mix or leverage. | Historical **PIT snapshots**, time-aware updates. |
| **Wrong covariance horizon** | A daily risk forecast need not be calibrated for the next 30 minutes; position sizing can be wrong even when factor labels are sensible. | Horizon-matched **intraday covariance calibration**. |

Avoiding open/close reduces some trading frictions and seasonality, **not** sector shocks, factor crowding, intraday announcements, or residual covariance. More factors are not automatically better: correlated/unstable factors and poor PIT data can *increase* estimation error. We need **adequate coverage + robust estimation + out-of-sample evidence**, not maximum complexity.

## 3. Factor model approaches — advantages and problems

| Model family | Main advantages | Main problems / verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Commercial fundamental multi-factor** (Barra, FactSet, Axioma, Bloomberg, Northfield) | Rich market/industry/style exposures; interpretable hedges; risk decomposition and, depending on product, factor covariance and specific risk. | Licensing; PIT history/export often separate; vendor horizons not necessarily 30 minutes. **Preferred if accessible.** |
| **Self-built institutional-style fundamental** (WRDS + intraday prices) | Customizable, interpretable, reproducible; supports PIT risk controls and consistent 30-minute factor returns. | Data engineering for filings, identifiers, delistings, factor standardization and industry constraints; needs covariance and specific-risk estimation. **Strong fallback, not trivial.** |
| **Statistical latent-factor** (PCA, PPCA, Factor Analysis; POET extension) | Discovers shared risks without a vendor taxonomy; POET can retain sparse residual correlations. | Factor rotation/instability, missing data, weak interpretability, possible mismatch with economically desired neutrality. **Useful benchmark/overlay.** |
| **Conditional / dynamic factors** (Kalman, IPCA, state-space) | Exposures can vary through time; models changing characteristics or market regimes. | Higher tuning and estimation risk, extra data; IPCA is not an out-of-the-box intraday covariance model. **Optional upgrade.** |
| **Market-only / FF factors** | Transparent, low-cost, easy to reproduce. | Omitted industry/style risks; public FF factor returns are daily/monthly, not a complete 30-minute exposure/covariance feed. **Sanity-check baseline only.** |


## 4. Where can we actually get the model?

**Commercial products (model-level data; not just generic market data):**

| Source | What is offered / advantage | Limitations and our access status |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **[MSCI Barra](https://www.msci.com/data-and-analytics/factor-investing/equity-factor-models)** | Established U.S. and global equity models; market/industry/style and trading-horizon variants; exposures and risk data via licensed distribution. | Commercial; **no Columbia model-data entitlement verified**. |
| **[FactSet Equity Risk Model](https://www.factset.com/marketplace/catalog/product/factset-equity-risk-model-global)** | Feed explicitly lists exposures, factor covariance, factor returns, residual risk, correlated specific risk. | **Current account: “Risk – Equity (FactSet)” template says contact representative; Create New disabled.** Historical bulk/API rights unknown. |
| **[SimCorp Axioma](https://www.simcorp.com/solutions/axioma-solutions/axioma-factor-risk-models/axioma-equity-factor-risk-models)** | Fundamental and statistical models; ultra-short/short/medium variants; vendor advertises U.S. model history since **1982**. | Commercial; no Columbia entitlement verified. **Ultra-short does not imply an exact 30-minute covariance**. |
| **[Bloomberg MAC3 / PORT](https://professional.bloomberg.com/products/risk/mac3/)** | Style/industry risk, multiple horizons, factor exposures/returns and covariance in separate machine-readable **Risk Model Files** service. | Columbia has **on-campus Bloomberg terminals**; terminal access ≠ licensed MAC3 file/API export. Bulk history not confirmed. |
| **[Northfield](https://www.northinfo.com/resource-details.php?id=2)** | U.S. fundamental multi-factor risk model with beta, fundamental characteristics and industry groups. | Commercial; PIT history, model variants and Columbia access must be checked. |

**Academic / open alternatives:**

| Source | What we can obtain | Why it is *not* equivalent to a purchased model feed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Columbia WRDS](https://guides.library.columbia.edu/WRDS/collection)**: CRSP, Compustat, TAQ | Historical constituents/identifiers, fundamental descriptors, corporate actions and intraday trades/quotes, subject to individual dataset rights. | **Inputs for building** a full factor model, *not* precomputed $B,\Omega,D$; PIT linking and release lags are our responsibility. |
| **[Kenneth French Data Library](https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/data_library.html)**; [AQR datasets](https://www.aqr.com/Insights/Datasets) | Public research factor-return series and portfolio benchmarks. | Not historical **stock-level PIT factor exposures**, specific risk, or 30-minute factor-return panels. |
| **[OpenFactor](https://github.com/ralliesai/openfactor)** / **[riskprism](https://github.com/wanxinwanxin/risk-prism)** | Public open-source examples with factor exposures / risk artifacts for supported U.S. equities. | Useful for architecture or demos; **not verified to cover a survivorship-free 2010–2025 PIT history**. Validate methodology, provenance and licensing. |
